step_by_step_reasoning: Nodes: the 9 world-model entities are kept one-to-one (two client actors, CDN as ThirdParty, S3, AppSync, API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB). No fusion or expansion was needed; Lambda is a single logical unit shared by all channels. Flows from the transcript: Flow 0 = tenant onboarding wizard and the identical check-in path (client -> CDN -> AppSync -> Lambda -> SQS fan-out -> Lambda reprocess -> DynamoDB). Flow 1 = third-party reseller/OTA channel (API client -> CDN -> API Gateway REST -> same Lambdas, response back through the CDN). Flow 2 = customer website journey (client -> CDN -> S3 static content -> CDN -> client, then the dynamic content path with direct DynamoDB resolvers returning data to AppSync and AppSync replying through the CDN). Ledger self-check: visual_connections has 16 entries and 16 edges are emitted, one per entry with the same source and target, including both directions for bidirectional pairs and the duplicated UserConsumerMobile -> CDN pair as two separate flow steps. No extra edges were added beyond the ledger.

graph.name: Anchor: Multi-Tenant Serverless Ticketing Platform
graph.notes: Anchor is a ticketing platform with more than 40 tenants (20+ onboarded in the last six months) for daytime experiences such as Statue of Liberty cruises, Niagara Falls, Alcatraz Island and NYC Ferry. Omni-channel: mobile app, website and third-party resellers (OTAs such as Expedia, Viator, GetYourGuide). Fully serverless: CDN, S3 static hosting, AppSync GraphQL, API Gateway REST, Lambda, SQS and DynamoDB with tenant partition keys.

nodes.name: UserConsumerMobile
nodes.notes: Tenants using the onboarding wizard web application and customers using the mobile app or website; also the mobile check-in application that looks up bookings and scans tickets.

nodes.name: UserConsumerAPI
nodes.notes: Third-party resellers / OTAs (e.g., Expedia, Viator, GetYourGuide) selling the offerings through a third-party REST API implemented for them.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: S3 bucket serving as an HTTP server for static content: event descriptions, ticket offering and pictures.

nodes.name: AppSync
nodes.notes: GraphQL gateway. Resolvers invoke Lambda; direct DynamoDB resolvers are also used and can be mapped and reused through AppSync pipeline resolvers.

nodes.name: ApiGateway
nodes.notes: Regular REST endpoint for resellers/OTAs; hits the same Lambdas used by the owned mobile app and website channels.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Holds fan-out messages for tenant setup subroutines and post check-in work (customer service, post-experience, review reminder email) that Lambda processes later.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Shared business logic for tenants and customers, invoked through AppSync and API Gateway. Fans out to subroutines by sending SQS messages and later reprocesses them; interacts with DynamoDB.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores all tenant data. Multi-tenancy: tables are shared and everything is partitioned by tenant using partition keys.

nodes.name: CDN
nodes.notes: CDN, the first thing every client request hits. Returns static content from S3 and routes dynamic requests to AppSync or API Gateway.

edges.notes: Tenant wizard web application (or check-in app) request first hits the CDN.
CDN forwards the dynamic request to AppSync, the GraphQL gateway.
AppSync resolvers invoke Lambda to process the GraphQL node and fan out to subroutines.
Lambda sends a set of SQS messages (tenant setup fan-out, post check-in tasks).
Messages are later processed by Lambda (e.g., sending the review reminder email after check-in).
Lambda interacts with DynamoDB to finish setting up the tenancy; data is partitioned by tenant.
Reseller / OTA request first hits the CDN.
CDN routes the reseller request to the REST endpoint on API Gateway.
API Gateway hits the same Lambdas used by the other channels.
Response returned to the reseller through the CDN.
Customer starts the journey on the website or mobile app; the request first hits the CDN.
CDN requests the static content hosted on the S3 bucket.
S3 serves the event descriptions and pictures to the CDN.
CDN returns the content to the client so the customer can browse and navigate.
Dynamic content: direct DynamoDB resolvers return data to AppSync, reusable through pipeline resolvers.
AppSync returns the GraphQL response for dynamic content through the CDN.
